definition: A sigmoid function is any mathematical function whose graph has a characteristic S-shaped or sigmoid curve.
details: A common example of a sigmoid function is the logistic function. Other sigmoid functions are given in the Examples section. In some fields, most notably in the context of artificial neural networks, the term "sigmoid function" is used as a synonym for "logistic function". Special cases of sigmoid functions include the Gompertz curve (used in modeling systems that saturate at large values of x) and the ogee curve (used in the spillway of some dams). Sigmoid functions have domain of all real numbers, with return (response) value commonly monotonically increasing but could be decreasing. Sigmoid functions most often show a return value (y axis) in the range 0 to 1. Another commonly used range is from −1 to 1. There is also the Heaviside step function, which instantaneously transitions between 0 and 1. A wide variety of sigmoid functions including the logistic and hyperbolic tangent functions have been used as the activation function of artificial neurons. Sigmoid curves are also common in statistics as cumulative distribution functions (which go from 0 to 1), such as the integrals of the logistic density, the normal density, and Student's t probability density functions. explainer.lead: A sigmoid function is any mathematical function whose graph has a characteristic S-shaped curve. It matters because S-shaped responses model saturation and switching across many fields.

tiers.eli5: It is any curve shaped like a stretched letter S, rising slowly, then quickly, then slowly again.
tiers.practitioner: In neural networks the term is often used as a synonym for the logistic function, a common example. A pitfall is assuming every S-shaped function is the logistic one.
tiers.paperLevel: Sigmoid functions have the domain of all real numbers; common examples include the logistic function, the Gompertz curve, used where systems saturate at large x, and the ogee curve, used in some dam spillways.

explainer.example: The logistic function is the standard sigmoid example, while the Gompertz curve is a special case used to model systems that saturate at large values of x.
